text:
Incident Bot: ALERT P0 - elevated tail latency on /v1/generate across hosted region-us-west-2. 90th p99 > 3s, error spike 5xx starting at 2024-03-14T11:07:14Z. Paging Maya (oncall). :rotating_light:
Maya (oncall): acked. looking now. any customer reports?
Sam Chen: i'm seeing increased 504s in the logs. top upstream is 'inference-runtime-gpu'. sending logs to #eng-runtime.
Alex R.: adding context: we rolled the runtime kernel changes about 30m before alert. could be regression on kernel selection.
Maya (oncall): quick mitigation options: 1) failover routing to dedicated cluster, 2) rollback runtime container to previous image, 3) scale up nodes. recommend failover first to stop customer impact quickly.
Julie - SRE: i'm on scaling now (doubling pool). if failover is faster Maya i can also start a rollback job.
Maya (oncall): @ops-bot run failover --to=dedicated-pool-usw2 --selector=blue-canary
ops-bot: Executing failover request: job id 3157. Estimated 45s to route traffic. Logging events to /ops/failovers/3157.
Maya (oncall): routing in progress...
Alex R.: while that's happening, can someone capture the KV cache hit rate and prefix cache metrics? if cache churn increased that's another signal.
Sam Chen: pulling metrics: prefix_cache_hit dropped from 92% -> 44% around the same time. cache evictions spiked. sending graph: https://grafana.redwood/inference/graphs/abc123
Luis - Product: any idea which customers impacted? we should line up comms if AcmeCorp or BigRetail are affected.
Maya (oncall): quick hit: we saw 20k failed requests in last 20m, traffic patterns show most from retriever pipelines (higher seq lengths). mapping to customers now.
Julie - SRE: failover completed. ops-bot reports traffic now served from dedicated-pool-usw2, routing delay cleared, 5xx rate down to baseline.
ops-bot: Failover job 3157 complete. New routing policy id: rp-20240314-3157.
Maya (oncall): confirming: p95 latency back to 180ms, p99 back to 400ms. marking incident mitigated.
Incident Bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED — P0 cleared. Start post-incident review? Use /postmortem create or schedule.
Maya (oncall): yes please. I'll kick off the postmortem. tagging ppl who should attend: @Alex R., @Julie - SRE, @Sam Chen, @Luis - Product.
Sam Chen: main findings so far: kernel-selection change + cache-eviction behavior under long sequence workloads. rollback or canary should've tripped earlier. we need better automated canary checks for cache pressure.
Alex R.: agreed. propose short-term action items: 1) add an automated healthcheck that measures prefix_cache_hit and flags canary if drop > 10% within 15m, 2) add an automated rollback for kernel changes if healthcheck fails, 3) update runbook for failover steps and verify docs.
Luis - Product: also want SLA impact calc for customers: can ops produce a per-customer failed-request count and expected credits owed? we'll prepare comms.
Maya (oncall): Sam can you assemble a minimal incident timeline and provide the failing commit/image? I can open the postmortem doc and assign owners.
Sam Chen: on it. suspected image: inference-runtime:2024-03-14-kernel-v2. commit abc9f2. timeline in progress.
Julie - SRE: i'll create a short checklist for on-call steps so handoffs are consistent. Also propose an improvement: postmortem skeleton auto-populated with mitigation timeline, graphs, and action-item placeholders (owner + due date).
Maya (oncall): agree. we should reduce friction between mitigation and postmortem creation. ops-bot, can we automate creation of a postmortem draft whenever Incident Bot posts MITIGATED for P0? include basic fields: summary, timeline, impact, root cause hypothesis, action items.
ops-bot: New request queued: create-postmortem-draft. Endpoint: /postmortems/drafts/create.
Maya (oncall): perfect. For this incident please: create draft, pre-fill mitigation timeline (failover job id, rollback candidates, metrics snapshot), and add tag 'pager-procedure'.
ops-bot: Draft created: https://pm.redwood/postmortems/drafts/20240314-3157 (private). Owners auto-assigned: Maya (oncall) - lead, Sam Chen - technical lead, Julie - SRE - ops remediation, Luis - Product - customer comms.
Alex R.: adding tooling wishlist for postmortems: - webhook from incident bot to create draft + copy critical graphs - integrate with action-item dashboard so items surface in weekly ops review - ability to auto-schedule postmortem meeting (Doodle-like) and ping participants
Sam Chen: technical: also want an automated 'regression detector' that runs after each runtime canary comparing prefix cache metrics, token latency, and error rate against baseline and opens a rollback PR if thresholds exceeded.
Luis - Product: timeline for comms: we need a customer-impact table with customers, failed-req count, window, and recommended statement. can we get that in next 4h?
Maya (oncall): Sam + Julie own the per-customer impact export. target 4h. Sam do you accept?
Sam Chen: accept.
Julie - SRE: accept. i'll also start a ticket to add the automated canary healthcheck into our deployment pipelines.
Maya (oncall): Action items recap (from thread):
- Sam Chen: produce timeline + failing image + per-customer failed-request export (due: today +4h)
- Julie - SRE: add on-call checklist, create ticket for automated canary healthcheck (due: 1 week)
- Alex R.: prototype regression-detector design doc (due: 2 weeks)
- Luis - Product: draft customer comms once Sam provides table (due: +6h)
- Ops: make postmortem draft public to postmortem channel and schedule meeting (owner: Maya) (due: tomorrow)

Maya (oncall): I'll also schedule a 45m postmortem review for tomorrow 09:30 PT and post in #postmortems. if folks can't make, ops-bot will gather asynchronous notes.
ops-bot: Meeting created: 2024-03-15 09:30 PT. Calendar link: https://calendar.redwood/meet/pm-20240315-09-30.
Incident Bot: NOTE: P0 postmortem required per policy. Reminder: complete within 7 days.
Maya (oncall): for the tooling improvements, can we create a small spike to evaluate options (concourse tasks, a small lambda, or integrating with our infra bot)? i'll put a 2-sprint proposal in planning.
Alex R.: I'll draft the spike scope, include cost/complexity tradeoffs and a demo of an automated rollback PR.
Julie - SRE: Quick snippet for the rollback job (for runbook):
```
# rollback to previous image
kubectl set image deploy/inference-runtime inference-runtime=inference-runtime:2024-03-01-stable
kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-runtime -w
```

Sam Chen: noted. i'll attach logs and the relevant grafana panels to the postmortem draft.
Maya (oncall): thanks all. closing here but leaving the postmortem draft open for edit. please update with any additional data points. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: created ticket OPS-2248 "Postmortem: kernel selection regression / cache eviction" and linked to draft. Ticket: https://tracker.redwood/OPS-2248
Luis - Product: will prepare a short customer-facing note after Sam's export.
Alex R.: one last thing: let's add a metric in the console showing live 'prefix_cache_hit' per model so product can see at-a-glance regressions. putting that on my radar.
Maya (oncall): good call. meeting tomorrow. end thread.
